description: ol-reserved-word (issue #837, maintainer ruling #833): the boundaries of binding, now that binding a built-in name is unconditionally free (spec/grammar.md:363, :386). Under issue #739 this fixture expected exactly one finding, at `:repeat = [1 2]`. It expects none. What it still pins is that the OTHER two boundaries never depended on that rule and are unchanged: (1) `:count = 3` (the Core primitive `count`) and `:helper = 4` (a procedure declared in this same program) are bindings, and spec/grammar.md:406 keeps variables out of the one callable namespace primitives, user procedures, and struct constructors share, so they shadow nothing; (2) a write INTO an existing value introduces no name, so `:repeat[1] = 5` on line 8 is data, not a declaration -- spec/grammar.md:404, "a postfix names a field or key, which is data". Eight lines, six top-level statements, zero findings. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) -- nothing is executed and no events are produced.
